newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Wing Tiek to sell steel firm stake.
newsitem.headline: Wing Tiek to sell steel firm stake.

text.p: Diversified Malaysian industrial group Wing Tiek Holdings Bhd said on Wednesday that it has reached agreement with Hottick Investment Ltd to divest its entire 69.2 percent interest in the National Steel Corp (NSC) of the Philippines for 12.17 billion pesos.

The divestment took into account its outstanding financial obligation of 336.7 million ringgit to pay for its stake in NSC under an agreement signed with the National Development Co of the Philippines on October 14, 1994, Wing Tiek managing director Joseph Chong said in a statement.

It also took into account the current debt level of the group and a potential financial obligation of a further 314.1 million ringgit under the second option to acquire up to 95 percent stake in NSC, he said.
Chong said Hottick had undertaken to pay the outstanding amount and assume Wing Tiek's remaining rights and obligations.

Other factors cited for the divestment were the expected reduction in import duties on protected items to a minimum of three percent in the Philippines by 2000 which would exert downward pressure on the pricing of NSC products and adversely affect its profitability.

Chong said the world steel price had remained subdued since the last quarter of 1995 and there was no sign of recovery in the short or medium term, resulting in NSC declaring a loss of 127 million pesos for the nine months to September 30, 1996.
The uncertain timing of flotation as a result of the adverse factors would further strain the financial resources and cashflow position of Wing Tiek, he added.

For Wing Tiek, the proposed divestment would result in an extraordinary gain of 97 million ringgit for the financial year ending July 31, 1997, but after taking into consideration interest and other expenses, it was expected to result in an estimated extraordinary loss of about 70 million ringgit.
Group net tangible assets per share would decrease to an estimated 1.67 ringgit from 2.70 ringgit as at July 31, 1996.

NSC was previously a Philippine government-owned company in which Wing Tiek bought the stake earlier this year. It produces more than 40 percent of the Philippines' steel output with annual capacity of 3.5 million tonnes.
